title: Storage phase 1: keep large files in a chunk store
prompt:
Implement phase 1 of docs/storage.md ("Chunk store; large files kept"). Read docs/storage.md first: it is the intended design, and this task is its phase 1 only (no R2, no streams). Phase 2a is already on main (fork with `start {"from": <agent or commit>}`, main merged into idle branches, branches pushed to spawn/<agent>): build on it, and keep the trailer through those paths, so that a fork from any checkpoint materializes that checkpoint's large files.

Today a file over LARGE_FILE_BYTES (8 MiB, crates/spawn-host/src/git.rs) stays out of the checkpoint commit and is lost when the workspace is unmounted. Required behaviour after this task:

1. A large file an engine writes in its workspace survives the end of the execution: when the session is resumed (or the agent's branch is mounted again), the file is back in the fresh mount, byte for byte, before the engine starts.
2. Large files never go into git. Text (every file up to 8 MiB) stays in git exactly as today. The bare repository must not grow by anything near a large file's size, and no blob over 8 MiB may appear on an agent's branch. Landing is unchanged and text only: large files never reach main.
3. A chunk-store port (a trait in spawn-core next to the other ports) with a local-directory adapter: content-defined chunks (FastCDC or equivalent), each named by the BLAKE3 hash of its bytes, compressed with zstd, written atomically (temporary file, then rename; an existing object is never rewritten), and verified on read (a chunk or manifest whose bytes do not hash to its name is an error; wrong bytes must never be written into a workspace, and a large file is materialized atomically too). Identical chunks are stored once, so a 1 MiB in-place edit of a 20 MiB file adds about a megabyte to the store, not the file again. Objects are immutable and nothing is deleted in this phase (no garbage collection): every checkpoint ever made stays restorable, and every non-empty file in the store directory is an object that never changes or disappears (temporary files are removed after the rename; a lock file, if any, stays empty).
4. The large-file manifest (path, mode, size, chunk list) is itself an object in the chunk store, and the checkpoint commit names it with a `Spawn-Large: <manifest hash>` trailer in its message. The branch head alone is the whole workspace. A checkpoint where only a large file changed is a new commit with the same tree and a new trailer; a checkpoint where nothing changed (text or large) makes no commit, as today. Only large files whose size or mtime changed since the last checkpoint are re-chunked (the kept index is the stat cache for text; keep the equivalent for large files). Mount reads the trailer of the branch head and materializes the large files again.
5. Where the chunk store lives is configurable: the environment variable SPAWN_CHUNK_STORE names its directory; without it the store defaults to a directory under the workspace root (e.g. <root>/.chunks) that mount and unmount never clear and that never becomes part of any workspace tree. Keep the adapter behind the port so phase 3 can add an R2 adapter without touching the Bridge or the git workspace store.

Update docs/storage.md (phase 1 done, the "Where state lives today" row for large files) and the doc comments in git.rs that say large files are lost at unmount. Add unit tests for the chunker, the store (round trip, dedup, a corrupted chunk is refused) and the manifest/trailer handling.

The gate judges this with rsi/scenarios/003.sh (read it): a fake Claude engine writes a 20 MiB file and a text file, exits, and the session is resumed; the large file must be back (sha256), the bare repository must grow by less than 2 MiB, the head commit must carry a Spawn-Large trailer, and SPAWN_CHUNK_STORE must hold the chunks; then a 1 MiB in-place edit, checkpointed when the engine exits, must be a commit with the same tree and a new trailer, the repository still under 2 MiB of growth, the chunk store under 8 MiB of growth, and the edited file back after another resume; a second agent started with `from` = the first checkpoint's commit id must get the original bytes in its fresh mount; every non-empty file the store held after the first checkpoint must still be there byte for byte after the edit and the fork; finally, with every file in the chunk store corrupted, a resume under a fresh, empty workspace root (same repository and chunk store) must never put wrong bytes in the large file (failing the mount, or leaving the file out, is acceptable). The scenario exits 0 when every check passes, 1 when an assertion fails, 2 on a harness or infrastructure failure.

Rules: never edit rsi/, scripts/rsi/, scripts/blackbox/ or scripts/mvp-e2e.sh (the gate rejects any change there). The gate also rejects fewer runnable tests than the base (do not delete, ignore or disable tests), any lint relaxation ([lints] tables, clippy.toml, new crate-level #![allow]/#![expect], a removed #![warn]/#![deny]), and any build-time code (build.rs, .cargo/, a `build =` key in a Cargo.toml). The gate builds offline from the cargo caches already on the host: a new crate builds only if it is already in ~/.cargo/registry. blake3 1.8.7 and zstd 0.14.3 are cached and build offline; fastcdc is not, so write the content-defined chunker yourself (a gear-hash FastCDC is a few dozen lines). All existing checks must still pass: clippy, the workspace tests, the e2e, the black-box scenarios and the web build.
